name: La Reine Marlene - SIA Project 23 24
description:
Information Systems - academic year 23/24
Course Project
Scenario

La Reine Marlene is a company specialized in the sale of materials and products for the home. To improve the efficiency of its operations and the service to customers, the company is re-designing its information system. The details follow.

La Reine Marlene has a wide network of suppliers. The suppliers of La Reine Marlene will have to register in the system, providing their credentials and company details, including VAT number, address and the IBAN for payments. Registered suppliers can make proposals of their own products by entering in the system the following information for each product: category, sale price (the one that La Reine Marlene must pay to the supplier), availability, photo, description, guaranteed delivery time. The product categories are 16: Garden, Bathroom, Air Conditioning, Lighting, Decoration, Flooring, Doors and Windows, Carpentry, Kitchen, Storage, Tools, Electricity, Construction, Paints, Hardware, Furniture. Once a proposal has been entered, the supplier can no longer modify it until they receive a response notification.

When a supplier enters a proposal, the administration department of La Reine Marlene receives a message notifying the presence of a new proposal from the suppliers. At that point, it must verify the proposal and select one of the following options: Order accepted, Revisions requested, Order rejected. If the order is accepted, a separate order management process will start, to which the information on the price to be displayed in the store is added, so that this information will already be available in the subsequent processes. If instead revisions have been requested, they must be made explicit in a comment: at that point the supplier receives a notification and has 5 working days to modify the proposal, entering reply comments, and re-submit it. If the proposal has been modified within the 5 working days, then the proposal evaluation process restarts, otherwise the proposal is deleted from the system and the supplier notified. The administrators receive a reminder every 48 hours about the presence of a proposal that is waiting to be validated. A proposal that has not been verified within 10 working days is automatically rejected, and a specific message is sent to the supplier.

Once the products ordered from the suppliers are shipped and arrive at the destination La Reine Marlene site (there are dozens of them throughout Italy), they are entered in the inventory of all the products available in the store (La Reine Marlene has no warehouse: any available product is on display). Each product is catalogued according to its category, available quantity and location in the store. The location in the store is entered directly by the goods receiving staff: when an order is delivered, the staff members must verify each product. If there are no problems, the operator confirms the product and the system proposes a list of possible placements: the location is chosen, and the product is physically handed over to whoever will take care of its placement in the store and of printing the price to be displayed. Should there be problems with any product, the operator reports it by entering a comment and the product does not enter the store. At the end of these operations of verification of an order arrival, the operator closes the procedure and a new process starts, managed by the order department: if all the products have been accepted, the order is concluded and the payment sent. Otherwise, the order is updated and a new arrival that completes it is awaited. In both cases specific messages are sent to the supplier.

The system keeps track of stock in real time. An automatic notification is sent to the order department when a product reaches a critical reorder level (where it is specified). The administrators, in fact, can schedule automatic reordering and replenishment actions for specific products, in order to maintain an optimal inventory. In case of automatic reordering, a message is sent to the pre-established supplier, who has two working days to confirm acceptance of the order. In the absence of critical thresholds and of the related automation, the new order is managed by the order department with a separate process.

Customers looking for materials for the home can purchase the products both through the physical store and through the online store. In the online store, customers who have registered on the site can browse the digital catalogue, specify the desired products and quantities and complete the order. The system automatically calculates the order total, including taxes and shipping costs. Customers can choose among different payment options: credit card (Visa or Mastercard), Paypal, Satispay, the La Reine Marlene purchasing card, or immediate online bank transfer with the affiliated banks. Once the order is paid, the system keeps track of deliveries in real time. Customers receive a link by email through which they can follow the status of their shipments. In addition, those who have given consent to the use of the mobile phone number will receive notifications on updates to delivery times. Once the product arrives at its destination, the order is tracked as concluded. Deliveries are managed by partner companies, and each online purchase is randomly assigned to a shipping carrier. Consider that the online store is also accessible through a dedicated app: the operations and procedures are the same as those of the site.

La Reine Marlene offers a complete customer service through the information system. Customers can ask questions, request assistance or make complaints directly through the system. Support tickets are automatically assigned to a customer service agent. Every time a ticket is assigned, the agent receives a notification and has 24 hours to respond (if this does not happen, the ticket is reassigned to a new operator, and the statistics updated). The customer is informed upon receipt of the reply message, and has five working days to respond: otherwise, the ticket is considered closed.

Finally, the system collects data on orders, sales, inventory, customer support. These data are used to analyze performance and make strategic decisions.
highLevelGoals: The supplier aims to efficiently submit product proposals, including all necessary details, and receive timely feedback on their status.
The supplier seeks to modify and resubmit proposals within the stipulated timeframe when revisions are requested, ensuring their products can be considered for order.
The supplier desires clear and prompt notifications regarding the acceptance, rejection, or request for revisions of their product proposals.
The supplier aims for a straightforward and secure registration process to provide their credentials and company details.
The administration department staff aims to efficiently verify product proposals, make informed decisions (accept, reject, request revisions), and initiate subsequent processes.
The administration department staff seeks to process all incoming proposals within defined timeframes to avoid automatic rejections and maintain operational efficiency.
The administration department staff aims to clearly communicate revision requests and comments to suppliers to facilitate accurate modifications.
The goods receiving staff aims to accurately verify delivered products, update inventory, and assign correct store locations.
The goods receiving staff seeks to efficiently report any issues or problems with delivered products to prevent them from entering the store inventory.
The goods receiving staff aims for a seamless handover process for products accepted into inventory, including printing price labels and physical placement.
The order department staff aims to effectively conclude orders, process payments to suppliers, and manage partial order arrivals.
The order department staff seeks to maintain optimal inventory levels through automatic reordering and replenishment actions, preventing stockouts.
The order department staff aims to receive timely confirmation from suppliers for automatically generated reorders to ensure continuous supply.
The customer aims to easily browse the digital catalogue, discover desired products, and specify quantities for purchase.
The customer seeks secure and diverse payment options to complete their online orders conveniently.
The customer desires real-time tracking of their orders and deliveries, including status updates and estimated arrival times.
The customer aims to easily ask questions, request assistance, or make complaints and receive timely and effective responses.
The customer service agent aims to promptly respond to assigned support tickets and effectively resolve customer inquiries, assistance requests, or complaints.
The customer service agent seeks an efficient system for managing assigned tickets, including notifications and automatic reassignment if response times are not met.
The customer service agent aims to clearly communicate responses and updates to customers regarding their support tickets.
